story: My company has not paid my salary for August and September 2026. It was Rs 35,000 a month. I resigned on 30 September 2026.

timeline.user_words: My company has not paid my salary for August and September 2026. It was Rs 35,000 a month.

facts.user_goal: Get unpaid salary for August and September 2026

rules.name: wage_due_date
rules.message: After your last day (30 Sep 2026), the law says final wages must be paid within two working days - about 03 Oct 2026 (not counting Sundays and national holidays; your State can set a different limit).
rules.label: When final pay was due

rules.name: wage_claim_limitation
rules.message: File your wage claim before 07 Sep 2029 (1034 days left). This counts 3 years from 07 Sep 2026 (when August 2026 wages fell due; each later month has its own, later deadline). Don't wait for the last date.
rules.label: Last date to file your wage claim

rules.name: where_to_claim
rules.message: You (or your union) can file a claim before the wage authority. For banks, railways, telecom, mines, insurance and central PSUs this is the Central Government's authority; for other employers it is your State labour department. It can order up to ten times the claim as compensation and recovers unpaid amounts like land revenue. The employer has to prove they paid you.
rules.label: Where to claim

rules.name: amount
rules.message: Unpaid wages: 2 month(s) x Rs 35,000 = Rs 70,000 (before any lawful deductions; HRA and overtime also count as wages for payment).
rules.label: Amount

answer.summary: You are owed Rs 70,000 for two months of unpaid salary. The law says your employer must pay this within two working days of your resignation. You can file a wage claim with your State labour department or the Central Government authority. You must file within three years of the wages falling due. The employer has to prove they paid you, and the claim authority can order up to ten times your amount as compensation.

claims.text: You are an employee under the Code on Wages, 2019.
Your unpaid wages for August and September 2026 total Rs 70,000.
Your employer must pay your final wages within two working days of your resignation on 30 September 2026.
You can file a wage claim within three years from 7 September 2026.
The employer must prove they paid you the wages.
Any contract or agreement you signed to give up your right to these wages is void.

next_steps.action: Gather proof of your employment and salary, like offer letters, payslips, and resignation letter.
next_steps.why: You need these to show the wage authority that you worked and what you were owed.

next_steps.action: File a wage claim with the labour department in your State or the Central Government authority if your company is a bank, railway, or telecom company.
next_steps.why: This is the correct place to recover your unpaid wages and ask for compensation.

next_steps.action: Do not wait until the last date to file your claim.
next_steps.why: The deadline is 7 September 2029, but you should file as soon as possible.

support.text: You are an employee under the Code on Wages, 2019.
support.reason: The law text defines 'employee' as any person employed on wages by an establishment to do work for hire or reward, which directly supports that the person is an employee under the Code on Wages, 2019. The sentence applies this definition to the person's own status.

support.text: Your unpaid wages for August and September 2026 total Rs 70,000.
support.reason: The law text defines 'wages' but does not state that unpaid wages for August and September 2026 total Rs 70,000. The sentence introduces specific amounts and months that are not in the law text. The law text only defines what wages means, not any specific unpaid amount or time period.

support.text: Your unpaid wages for August and September 2026 total Rs 70,000.
support.reason: The law text [LIM1963_art7] mentions 'Three years' and 'When the wages accrue due' but does not specify that the limitation period is three years from 7 September 2026. The sentence adds a specific date (7 September 2026) that is not in the law text, and the law text is incomplete/fragmentary. The sentence also doesn't clearly match the fragmentary text provided.

support.text: Your employer must pay your final wages within two working days of your resignation on 30 September 2026.
support.reason: The law text [COW2019_s17](2) explicitly states that where an employee 'has resigned from service...the wages payable to him shall be paid within two working days of his...resignation.' The sentence applies this rule to resignation on 30 September 2026, which is a permissible application of the legal rule to the person's own facts.

support.text: You can file a wage claim within three years from 7 September 2026.
support.reason: The law text [COW2019_s45](6) states the application may be filed 'within a period of three years from the date on which claims...arises.' The sentence specifies 'within three years from 7 September 2026,' which adds a specific date not in the law text. The law text does not mention '7 September 2026' as the date claims arise. The sentence appears to add a specific date that is not in the law text.

support.text: The employer must prove they paid you the wages.
support.reason: The law text [COW2019_s59] explicitly states 'the burden to prove that the said dues have been paid shall be on the employer' in cases of non-payment of wages. The sentence restates this legal rule: 'The employer must prove they paid you the wages.'

support.text: Any contract or agreement you signed to give up your right to these wages is void.
support.reason: The law text [COW2019_s60] explicitly states that 'Any contract or agreement whereby an employee relinquishes the right to any amount...under this Code shall be null and void.' The sentence restates this legal rule: 'Any contract or agreement you signed to give up your right to these wages is void.' The phrase 'these wages' is a permissible application of the legal rule to the person's own facts.

From: [FILL: your full name], [FILL: your full postal address]

I was employed with you at a monthly wage of Rs 35,000. My wages for August 2026 to September 2026 have not been paid. My last working day was 30 September 2026.

I request you to pay the unpaid amount of Rs 70,000 within 15 days of receiving this letter, to my bank account [FILL: account details].

If the amount is not paid, I intend to file a claim before the authority under the Code on Wages, 2019, which may also award compensation, without further notice to you.

Yours faithfully,
[FILL: your name and signature]

draft_notes:
How to send it:
1. Find their correct address in your offer letter, salary slip, or the company's registered office on the MCA website (mca.gov.in).
2. Fill every [FILL] slot. Remove anything that isn't true - only state facts you can prove.
3. Send by Speed Post and keep the receipt and the tracking proof of delivery. Also send a copy by email or WhatsApp and keep a screenshot.
4. Wait 15 days. Sending this letter does NOT stop any legal time limit - file your claim/complaint before the deadline shown, even if they haven't replied.
5. Free help to check the letter: legal aid 15100 or Tele-Law 14454.

Laws this letter relies on: Code on Wages, 2019, s.17(1)-(4) (Time limit for payment of wages); Code on Wages, 2019, s.45(1)-(6) (Claims authority, compensation, recovery and time limit); Code on Wages, 2019, s.59 (Burden of proof on employer); Code on Wages, 2019, s.2(d) (Central or State Government: whose authority applies); Code on Wages, 2019, s.2(y) (main part, clauses (a)-(j)) (What counts as "wages")
